sources.entry: PullBull - GitHub pull requests, issues and Projects boards in the menu bar. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/rustycamper/pullbull) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: PullBull is a read-only, keyboard-first macOS menu bar app for tracking GitHub pull requests, issues, and Projects boards.
summary.what_it_does: PullBull shows GitHub pull requests and issues in the macOS menu bar, split into tabs: Review (PRs waiting on you or your team), Mine (your open PRs with review state and checks), Team, Assigned, Created, and Board. Issues are grouped by Projects board Status when a board exists. Issue detail lists linked PRs. A search bar accepts @user, ~label, is:open/closed/merged/draft, status: filters, #number, and GitHub links, with Tab autocomplete and saved searches. Notifications can be toggled per event, including review requested, approved, changes requested, CI failed, new comment, merged, and issue assigned. An optional "Ask" feature uses the user's own Anthropic API key to find items from a plain-language description and is off by default. The README says it never writes to GitHub and has no telemetry or server.
use_cases: track pull requests waiting for my review
monitor my open PRs and CI checks from the menu bar
browse GitHub Projects board status without a browser
find a PR or issue by number or link quickly
get per-event GitHub notifications on a Mac
search GitHub issues by label, author, or board status
how_to_run: Or download the zip from Releases and move PullBull.app to /Applications
Sign in with GitHub via the PullBull for macOS app, or log in with the GitHub CLI using repo and read:org scopes
For Projects boards with gh: gh auth refresh -s read:project
notable: Keyboard-first with a global hotkey (⌃ ⌥ P) and type-anywhere search
Native SwiftUI and AppKit with no web views
Ask feature finds items from a description using the user's own Anthropic key, off by default
Tokens stored in Keychain on this Mac, or held in memory when using gh
caveats: Organization content needs a GitHub App installed by an org owner, or the gh read:project scope for boards
Ask feature requires the user's own Anthropic API key and sends data to Anthropic when used
Listed on awesome-mac under Version Control; the README does not state a maintenance status
